title: Venn: Resource Management for Collaborative Learning Jobs
problem: Multiple concurrent collaborative learning (federated learning) jobs compete for ephemeral, heterogeneous edge devices with overlapping eligibility requirements; existing schedulers use random device-to-job matching, causing high scheduling delays and poor job completion time.
motivation: CL jobs must wait for enough eligible devices (those meeting hardware/data/software constraints) to become available. Different jobs compete for overlapping subsets of devices. Random matching wastes scarce device types on jobs that have alternatives, extending average JCT up to the point where scheduling delay dominates over response collection time.
method: Venn is a centralized scheduler for federated learning that uses two algorithms. Intersection Resource Scheduling (IRS) groups jobs by device type, sorts jobs within each group by remaining work (shortest first), and allocates devices to the group with the most waiting jobs relative to available resources, prioritizing groups needing scarce hardware (O(max(m log m, n^2)) complexity). A tier-based matcher then partitions devices into V capability levels and randomly assigns jobs to tiers, only engaging tier-matching when it reduces job completion time (1 + c > V + c*g). Fairness logic adjusts job priorities to prevent starvation.
key_novelty: It formalizes and solves the Intersection Resource Scheduling problem for federated learning—where job device needs can overlap, contain, or nest within each other—using a strategy aware of device contention (how often multiple jobs need the same hardware) that jointly reduces job startup delays and response collection time.
contributions: Formalization of Intersection Resource Scheduling (IRS) problem for multi-CL-job contention
Two-level contention-aware scheduling heuristic (intra-group shortest-first + inter-group resource allocation)
Tier-based device-to-job matching reducing response collection time under low contention
Starvation prevention via fairness-weighted demand adjustment
Evaluation across 5 real-world CL workload scenarios with up to 1.88x JCT improvement

metrics.speedup: Up to 1.88x JCT improvement vs random matching baseline
metrics.accuracy: No impact on final model accuracy vs random matching
metrics.other: O(max(m log m, n^2)) scheduling complexity; negligible overhead at scale

limitations: Assumes synchronous CL training rounds (though authors note extension to async)
Device tier granularity V is a hyperparameter requiring tuning
Simulator-based evaluation; real-world large-scale deployment not shown
